claim: Of the 0.36 W of UV-C from the LEDs, 84.8 % enters the water and 52.9 % is absorbed by it at 90 %/cm
law: Conservation of radiant power in the Monte Carlo ray trace (absorbed + lost = entering)

claim: Reduction equivalent dose (RED) at 1.2 L/min and 90 %/cm reaches 40 mJ/cm2 for a 254 nm-equivalent response (laminar profile)
law: Fluence rate = absorbed power density / alpha; dose = fluence rate x residence time along each streamline; RED for a 20 mJ/cm2-per-log challenge organism

claim: Organism response at 275 nm is close enough to that at 254 nm that the RED stays above 40 mJ/cm2
law: Fluence-based rate constants of MS2: 280 nm LED 0.052 against LP lamp 0.056 cm2/mJ (ratio 0.93, taken for 275 nm though measured at 280 nm); E. coli 0.31 against 0.27 (Beck et al. 2017); RED x 0.93

claim: Even the least-dosed streamline (laminar, on the axis) gets the 4-log dose for Cryptosporidium and Giardia
law: 40 CFR 141.720(d)(1): 22 mJ/cm2 for 4-log Cryptosporidium and Giardia at 254 nm

claim: LumaFlow is not a virus barrier: 40 to 51 mJ/cm2 is far below the 186 mJ/cm2 for 4-log virus (adenovirus)
law: 40 CFR 141.720(d)(1) virus column: 39 mJ/cm2 for 0.5 log, 186 for 4 log
check: Non-claim kept in PRC, PRS and the safety notes; about 0.5 log of adenovirus at the design dose

claim: Bacteria do not regain viability by photoreactivation or dark repair after the design dose
law: Photorepair of UV-C damage is known in bacteria and is smaller at higher doses and at LED wavelengths near 280 nm (literature review in Beck et al. 2017); not quantified for this reactor
check: No calculation possible; plate counts with light and dark holding at TRL 4

claim: Water left standing in the reactor between draws does not regrow bacteria past the outlet, with the idle LED pulse of 10 s every 4 h
law: Biofilm regrows in stagnant point-of-use devices; the idle pulse gives the standing water about 38 mJ/cm2 volume-average per 10 s pulse (twice the 5 s run-on dose of LMF-CAL-001 D4; corrected after the independent review); downstream valve and tubing are not dosed

claim: The dose target is met even if the liner reflects only 0.80, as plain PTFE might, not 0.95
law: Ray trace rerun at a wetted reflectance of 0.80, times the 275 nm factor 0.93; reflectance of wetted sintered PTFE at 275 nm to be measured (the reviewer's trace needs about 0.72 or more)

claim: No UV-C falls on an elastomer: window gasket and sensor window washer
law: Photo-oxidation of EPDM under UV-C; ray trace of the light refracted outward in the window: 4.2 % of the LED output, 2.6 mW/cm2, about 856 J/cm2 a year on the gasket annulus
check: First run: EPDM in the light path (failed). Fix: both seals in food-contact expanded PTFE, which UV-C does not degrade

claim: UV-C passing through the 3 mm PTFE wall and top disc is too weak to degrade the acetal upper cap
law: Sintered PTFE is a diffuse reflector but not opaque at 3 mm; acetal yellows and embrittles under UV; diffuse transmittance of the liner grade at 275 nm is not published for this part
check: Measure the liner's transmittance at TRL 4; fallback: a 0.3 mm 316 foil cup in the liner pocket

claim: Quartz window 57 x 10 mm on a 51 mm seat stays below the 6.8 MPa design stress at 8 bar
law: Simply supported circular plate, sigma = 3 (3 + nu) p a^2 / (8 t^2); fused quartz design stress 6.8 MPa (Momentive)

claim: The 2 mm 316 retaining ring stays within 2/3 of its proof stress at the specified screw torque
law: Ring as a cantilever strip between the screw circle (65 mm) and the washer centre (54 mm), arm 5.5 mm; preload = T / (K d), K 0.13 to 0.16 with anti-seize; first run at 0.5 N m dry: 202 MPa (failed); 0.3 N m dry was 121 to 162 MPa (reviewer: too narrow a window)
closed_by: LMF-DEC-001 D-S2 (2026-10-25): 316 sheet, anti-seize, 0.21 N m; worst nut factor 0.13

claim: At 8 bar the window gasket keeps at least twice the water pressure as seating stress
law: Least preload 2.62 kN (0.21 N m, K 0.16) less the pressure load on the 50 mm seal (1.57 kN) over the 588 mm2 gasket

claim: M5 316 tie rods carry the end load at 8 bar within 0.6 of their proof stress
law: Stress = end load / (4 x 14.2 mm2); A4-70 proof stress 450 MPa (ISO 3506-1)

claim: Reactor tube hoop stress at 8 bar is a small share of the 316 proof stress
law: Thin-wall hoop stress p r / t; allowable 205 / 3

claim: Acetal roof over the liner pocket stays below its long-term design stress at 8 bar
law: Clamped circular plate, sigma = 0.75 p a^2 / t^2; acetal long-term design stress 10 MPa (assumed)

claim: LED board stays at or below 50 degC with continuous flow, at the worst film coefficient
law: Two thermal paths in parallel: finned sink to 30 degC air, spreader and 316 cap to 25 degC water

claim: LED junctions stay below an 85 degC rating
law: Board temperature + 10 K/W x 2.11 W per LED; 85 degC is a common junction limit for 3535 UV-C LEDs, to confirm on the chosen part

claim: The water warms by about 0.11 K carrying 8.9 W of LED heat
law: Q = m_dot cp dT at 1.2 L/min

claim: Thermal shock from 5 degC water on a warm window does not crack fused quartz
law: Fused silica expansion 0.55e-6 /K (Momentive); thermal stress E alpha dT / (1 - nu) for a 40 K step with E 72 GPa

claim: Flow in the 50 mm bore is laminar at 1.2 L/min (the profile itself is not known: see S34)
law: Re = rho U D / mu with D 50 mm; transition near 2,300

claim: Pressure drop stays below 0.5 bar at 1.2 L/min
law: dp = (Q / Kv)^2 per component: 0.15 bar on the assumed Kv 0.35 and 0.25, 0.39 with 0.2 and 0.15, 0.59 with a direct-acting valve of Kv 0.10 (independent review)
check: Depends on datasheet Kv; PR-008 at risk until the sensor and valve are chosen

claim: Mains power while water flows stays at or below 25 W
law: LED 6 x 350 mA x 6.2 V through a 90 % driver, valve 4.8 W, controller 0.6 W, adapter 88 %

claim: Standby power stays at or below 0.5 W
law: Flow sensor 75 mW, outlet pressure sensor 10 mW and MCU sleep through a 70 % light-load adapter, plus 0.1 W no-load

claim: The wall photodiode signal at the alarm threshold is well above the amplifier noise floor
law: Photocurrent at S/S_ref = 0.79 against 10 pA (a hundred times a SiC photodiode's dark current of about 0.1 pA through a transimpedance amplifier)

claim: LEDs switch on within 0.5 s of flow starting at 0.3 L/min
law: First pulse of a 15 Hz per L/min sensor plus 20 ms

claim: LED running hours do not limit life within 10 years of household use
law: 92 h a year (flow plus idle pulse) x 10 years against a 10,000 h rated life (L70 class, to confirm on the chosen part)

claim: The dose stays above 40 mJ/cm2 with the LEDs derated for junction temperature and bin
law: Nominal 47.3 mJ/cm2 (B10); with about 12 % less output near 62 degC and a 10 % low bin: 37.5 (B11); both factors typical, not yet from the chosen LED's datasheet
check: Closes when the LED is chosen; if the stack holds, routes to Amish (LMF-DEC-001 O-3)

claim: Mixing in the reactor leaves the RED between the plug and laminar limits
law: The laminar profile never develops (entrance length 1.3 m against 0.23 m), the inlet jet has a port Reynolds number of about 3,000 to 6,000 and the heated lower cap drives buoyant mixing (Richardson number about 6 to 12); a back-mixed reactor of 5 to 10 tanks in series would give 31 to 39 mJ/cm2 (reviewer's trace)
check: Residence-time distribution by tracer test at TRL 4 with the side inlet kept (O-4 (a), decided by Amish 2026-10-25); perforated PTFE inlet ring ready if the test shows strong back-mixing

claim: The water-film coefficient in the stainless lower cap bore is at least the 150 W/(m2 K) low end used for the board temperature
law: Developing laminar flow over the first 18 mm (Sieder-Tate, Nu = 1.86 Gz^(1/3), Gz = 9973); the fully developed value Nu 3.66 (h about 44) the reviewer used applies only far downstream

claim: Closing the outlet valve at full flow keeps the reactor within the 8 bar window rating
law: Joukowsky surge rho c v in the 1 m PE inlet tube (c about 400 m/s, v 0.63 m/s) added to the 4 bar limiter setting; a rigid copper line would add more, so the tube from the tee stays PE (BOM line 15)

claim: Opening the faucet starts the unit
law: First run: the normally closed valve sits downstream of the flow sensor, so with the faucet open and the valve shut no water flows and the flow sensor can never wake the controller (failed). Fix: an outlet pressure sensor between valve and faucet; the drop in line pressure starts the LEDs, then the valve opens and the flow sensor must confirm flow
check: Start-up sequence in LMF-CAL-001 D5; standby 0.23 W

claim: One failed LED of six trips the low-dose alarm
law: The wall sensor sees the six LEDs about equally: S/S_ref = 5/6 against the alarm threshold, now set from the 275 nm weighted RED (40 / 47.3)

claim: The SiC photodiode reads the UV-C, not the LEDs' longer-wavelength tail
law: SiC (band gap about 3.26 eV) has little response above about 380 nm; AlGaN LEDs emit a weak parasitic band near 300 to 400 nm that water hardly absorbs
check: Check against the chosen LED's spectrum and the photodiode's response curve

claim: Average dose of 75.4 mJ/cm2 at 90 %/cm and 1.2 L/min
law: Volume-average dose = absorbed power / (alpha Q), independent of geometry (the ray trace counts only the water between the ports, so it reads lower)

claim: Monte Carlo noise in the RED is under 3 %
law: Second run of 600,000 photons with another seed

claim: No mercury anywhere in the unit
law: AlGaN UV-C LEDs contain no mercury (Minamata Convention context in PRB)
check: Bill of materials review: no lamp, no mercury

claim: Every wetted material is suitable for food contact: 316, PTFE and expanded PTFE, fused silica, EPDM O-rings out of the light, acetal; and the bought parts on the water path (flow sensor, valve, pressure sensor, tee, tube, restrictor) in food-contact, lead-free grades
law: 21 CFR 177.1550 (perfluorocarbon resins), 177.2470 (acetal copolymer), 177.2600 (rubber articles); NSF/ANSI 61 certification to assess for the chosen grades
check: Reactor reviewed in the model; bought water-path parts to confirm at purchase (DEC To confirm); acetal is poorer in chloraminated water, which the well-water first user does not have

claim: No galvanic cell between the aluminium heat path and the 316 cap
law: Aluminium and 316 touch only through the thermal pads on the dry side; the reactor's wetted metal is all 316, and the valve, flow sensor and pressure sensor are specified with plastic or stainless wetted parts (no brass)
check: Design review of the joint stack

claim: A 0.8 m2 hollow-fibre cartridge passes 1.2 L/min at no more than 0.5 bar transmembrane pressure
law: Darcy flow through the membrane: flux 90 L/(m2 h) at 0.5 bar needs a clean-water permeability of 180 L/(m2 h bar); PVDF and PES UF membranes span roughly 100 to 500
check: To confirm on a cartridge datasheet; a larger cartridge if not

claim: Intact 0.01 to 0.02 um fibres remove bacteria (0.5 um and up) and protozoan cysts (3 um and up) by size
law: Size exclusion; US EPA Membrane Filtration Guidance Manual (EPA 815-R-06-009) credits log removal of Cryptosporidium only with direct integrity testing
check: Pore size 25 times smaller than the smallest bacteria

claim: Viruses (20 to 100 nm) are only partly removed
law: Virus sizes overlap the pore size; removal depends on the membrane grade

claim: A 1 bar air pressure-decay test finds a broken fibre without forcing air through intact pores
law: Young-Laplace bubble point 4 gamma / d for a 0.02 um pore (ASTM D6908 practice)

claim: The slim 10 in housing holds 8 bar
law: Catalogue housings are commonly rated near 8.6 bar (125 psi); to confirm on the chosen housing

claim: Treatment needs no power; fouling shows as a rising gap between the two gauges
law: Supply pressure drives the flow; TMP rises as the cake layer grows (Darcy)

claim: Twelve LEDs give an average dose of about 100 mJ/cm2 at 90 %/cm and 1.2 L/min
law: Absorbed share 29 % from single-pass absorption across the tube and a reflector of 0.80; average dose = absorbed power / (alpha Q); RED to come from a ray trace

claim: The RED of the radial reactor reaches 40 mJ/cm2
law: Laminar flow in a 20 mm tube (Re about 1,270) gives a reactor efficiency near 0.5, so RED about half the average
check: Ray trace needed before C could be chosen

claim: The quartz flow tube holds 8 bar
law: Hoop stress p r / t against the 6.8 MPa design stress

claim: LED strips stay at or below 50 degC with flow, cooled by their fins and through the end fittings into the water
law: 25.3 W through air (2.2 K/W) and water (0.76 K/W) paths in parallel from 25 degC water

claim: The seals at the tube ends stay out of UV-C guided along the quartz wall
law: Light trapped in the quartz wall by total internal reflection reaches its ends; PTFE-encapsulated O-rings there
check: By design in the option C model

claim: The same flow switch, dose photodiode and valve logic as option A work across a thin radial column
law: The photodiode in the reflector gap sees direct LED light as well as light through the water, so its signal depends less on UVT than option A's; mapping to assess
check: To assess if C is chosen
